summary: If someone promised "an issaron," he brings one; "issaronim," he brings two. If he forgot how many he said, he brings sixty. If he promised "a mincha," he may bring any kind; Rabbi Yehuda says he brings the mincha of fine flour.

chunks.en: "I take upon myself an issaron":
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a tenth of an ephah for a meal offering,

chunks.en: he must bring one.
chunks.st: must bring a meal offering of one-tenth.

chunks.en: "Issaronim": he must bring two.
chunks.st: If he says: It is incumbent upon me to bring tenths of an ephah, he must bring two-tenths, as that is the minimum plural amount.

chunks.en: "I said how many, but I do not know what I said":
chunks.st: If he says: I specified several tenths of an ephah but I do not know which number I specified,

chunks.en: he must bring sixty issaron.
chunks.st: he must bring sixty-tenths, as that is the maximum amount of a meal offering.
chunks.stMore: The flour beyond the amount that he actually specified is rendered a voluntary meal offering.

chunks.en: "I take upon myself a mincha":
chunks.st: If one says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a meal offering,

chunks.en: he may bring whichever kind he wants.
chunks.st: he may bring whichever meal offering that he wishes,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the fine-flour meal offering, the shallow-pan or deep-pan meal offering, or the meal offering baked in an oven in the form of loaves or wafers.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: He must bring the mincha of fine flour,
chunks.st: He must bring the fine-flour meal offering,

chunks.en: because it is the special one among the menachos.
chunks.st: as it is the most notable of the meal offerings.

summary: If someone promised "a mincha" or "menachos" and forgot what kind or how big, he must bring enough to be sure he kept his promise. Rebbi says he must bring sixty menachos of every size from one to sixty issaron.

chunks.en: "A mincha," or "a kind of mincha":
chunks.st: If one says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a meal offering, or: It is incumbent upon me to bring a type of meal offering,

chunks.en: he must bring one.
chunks.st: he must bring one meal offering.

chunks.en: "Menachos," or "a kind of menachos":
chunks.st: If he says: It is incumbent upon me to bring meal offerings, or: It is incumbent upon me to bring meal offerings of a certain type,

chunks.en: he must bring two.
chunks.st: he must bring two.

chunks.en: "I said which kind, but I do not know what I said":
chunks.st: If he says: I specified a meal offering but I do not know which meal offering I specified,

chunks.en: he must bring all five kinds.
chunks.st: he must bring all five types of meal offerings.

chunks.en: "I said a mincha of issaronim
chunks.st: If one says: I specified a meal offering of tenths of an ephah

chunks.en: but I do not know how many I said":
chunks.st: but I do not know how many tenths I specified,

chunks.en: he must bring a mincha of sixty issaron.
chunks.st: he must bring a meal offering of sixty-tenths of an ephah.

chunks.en: Rebbi says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:

chunks.en: He must bring menachos of issaronim
chunks.st: His obligation is satisfied only when he brings meal offerings of all sizes, in increments of tenths of an ephah,

chunks.en: from one up to sixty.
chunks.st: ranging from one-tenth of an ephah to sixty
chunks.stMore: -tenths, for a total of sixty meal offerings with a total volume of 1,830 tenths of an ephah, or 183 ephahs. He fulfills his vow with one of the meal offerings, and the rest are rendered voluntary meal offerings.

summary: If someone promised wood for the mizbeach, he gives at least two logs; frankincense, at least a handful. The mishnah lists five rules about a handful of frankincense.

chunks.en: "I take upon myself wood":
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate pieces of wood as fuel for the altar,

chunks.en: he must give no less than two logs.
chunks.st: must donate no fewer than two logs.

chunks.en: "Frankincense": no less than a handful.
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring frankincense, must bring no less than a handful.

chunks.en: There are five rules of handfuls:
chunks.st: The mishna states tangentially: There are five halakhot pertaining to handfuls.

chunks.en: One who says, "I take upon myself frankincense,"
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring an offering of frankincense,

chunks.en: may give no less than a handful.
chunks.st: may not bring less than a handful.

chunks.en: One who gives a mincha
chunks.st: One who pledges to bring a meal offering

chunks.en: must bring with it a handful of frankincense.
chunks.st: must bring with it a handful of frankincense.

chunks.en: One who offers the handful outside
chunks.st: One who intentionally offers up a handful of a meal offering outside the Temple courtyard is

chunks.he: חַיָּב. וּשְׁנֵי בְזִיכִין טְעוּנִין שְׁנֵי קֳמָצִים:
chunks.en: is punished. And the two bowls need two handfuls.
chunks.st: liable to receive excision from the World-to-Come [karet]. The two bowls of frankincense that accompany the shewbread are required to have two handfuls of frankincense.

summary: If someone promised gold, silver or copper to the Beis HaMikdash, he gives at least a certain amount. If he forgot how much he said, he keeps giving until he is sure he did not mean that much.

chunks.en: "I take upon myself gold":
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate gold to the Temple treasury,

chunks.en: no less than a gold dinar.
chunks.st: must give no less than a gold dinar.

chunks.en: "Silver": no less than a silver dinar.
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate silver to the Temple treasury, must give no less than the value of a silver dinar.

chunks.en: "Copper": no less than a silver ma'ah.
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate copper to the Temple maintenance, must give no less than the value of a silver ma’a.

chunks.en: "I said how much, but I do not know what I said":
chunks.st: One who says: I specified the amount of gold, silver, or copper, but I do not know what I specified,

chunks.en: he keeps bringing until he says,
chunks.st: must bring the maximum amount of gold, silver, or copper, until it reaches an amount where he says:

chunks.en: "I did not mean this much."
chunks.st: I am certain that I did not intend to donate that much.

summary: If someone promised wine for the mizbeach, he brings at least three log; oil, at least one log (Rebbi says three). If he forgot how much he said, he brings as much as is brought on the day with the most.

chunks.en: "I take upon myself wine":
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a libation of wine, must bring

chunks.en: no less than three log.
chunks.st: no less than three log,
chunks.stMore: as that is the minimum amount of wine brought as a libation accompanying an animal offering.

chunks.en: "Oil": no less than one log.
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring oil, must bring no less than a log, as the smallest meal offering includes one log of oil.

chunks.en: Rebbi says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:

chunks.en: Three log.
chunks.st: He must bring no less than three log,
chunks.stMore: as that is the amount of oil in the meal offering that accompanies the sacrifice of a lamb, which is the smallest amount in any of the meal offerings that accompany the sacrifice of an animal.

chunks.en: "I said how much, but I do not know what I said":
chunks.st: One who says: I specified how many log I vowed to bring but I do not know what amount I specified,

chunks.en: he brings as much as on the day with the most.
chunks.st: must bring an amount of oil equivalent to the amount brought on the day that the largest amount of oil is sacrificed in the Temple.

summary: If someone promised an olah, he brings a lamb; Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says a bird is enough. If he forgot what kind of animal he said, he must bring every kind it might have been.

chunks.en: "I take upon myself an olah":
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a burnt offering,

words.note: A korban that is burned completely on the mizbeach.

chunks.en: he must bring a lamb.
chunks.st: must bring a lamb, which is the least expensive land animal sacrificed as an offering.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: Or a turtledove or a young pigeon.
chunks.st: He may bring either a dove or a pigeon, as a bird burnt offering.

chunks.he: פֵּרַשְׁתִּי מִן הַבָּקָר וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מַה פֵּרַשְׁתִּי,
chunks.en: "I said it would be from the cattle, but I do not know what I said":
chunks.st: One who says: I vowed to bring a burnt offering, and I specified that it would be from the herd, but I do not know what animal I specified,

chunks.en: he must bring a bull and a calf.
chunks.st: must bring a bull and a male calf, as a burnt offering is brought only from male animals.

chunks.he: מִן הַבְּהֵמָה וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מַה פֵּרַשְׁתִּי,
chunks.en: "From the animals, but I do not know what I said":
chunks.st: One who says: I vowed to bring a burnt offering and I specified that it would be from the animals but I do not know what animal I specified,

chunks.he: יָבִיא פָר וָעֵגֶל אַיִל גְּדִי וְטָלֶה.
chunks.en: he must bring a bull, a calf, a ram, a goat, and a lamb.
chunks.st: must bring a bull and a male calf, a ram, a large male goat, a small male goat, and a male lamb.

chunks.en: "I said, but I do not know what I said":
chunks.st: One who says: I vowed to bring a burnt offering, and I specified what type of burnt offering it would be, but I do not know what I specified,

chunks.en: he adds a turtledove and a young pigeon to them.
chunks.st: adds a dove and a pigeon to the previous list.

summary: If someone promised a todah or shelamim, he brings a lamb. If he forgot what kind of animal he said, he must bring every kind it might have been, male and female.

chunks.en: "I take upon myself a todah,"
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a thanks offering

chunks.en: or "shelamim": he must bring a lamb.
chunks.st: and a peace offering, must bring a lamb, which is the least expensive land animal sacrificed as an offering.

chunks.he: פֵּרַשְׁתִּי מִן הַבָּקָר וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מַה פֵּרַשְׁתִּי,
chunks.en: "I said it would be from the cattle, but I do not know what I said":
chunks.st: One who says: I vowed to bring a peace offering and I specified that it would be from the herd but I do not know what animal I specified,

chunks.en: he must bring a bull and a cow, a male calf and a female calf.
chunks.st: must bring a bull and a cow, and a male calf and a female calf.

chunks.he: מִן הַבְּהֵמָה וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מַה פֵּרַשְׁתִּי,
chunks.en: "From the animals, but I do not know what I said":
chunks.st: One who says: I vowed to bring a burnt offering and specified that it would be from the animals, but I do not know what animal I specified,

chunks.en: he must bring a bull and a cow,
chunks.st: must bring a bull and a cow,

chunks.en: a male calf and a female calf,
chunks.st: a male calf and a female calf,

chunks.en: a ram and a ewe,
chunks.st: a ram and a ewe,

chunks.en: a young male goat and a young female goat, a grown male goat and a grown female goat,
chunks.st: a large, i.e., adult, male goat and a large female goat, a small, i.e., young, male goat and a small female goat,

chunks.en: a male lamb and a female lamb.
chunks.st: and a male lamb and a female lamb.

summary: If someone promised a bull, calf, ram or lamb, the animal with its nesachim must be worth a set amount. If he promised it worth a certain amount, the animal alone must be worth that. Two cheaper bulls do not count for one expensive one. A different color or a smaller animal does not count, but a bigger one does (Rebbi disagrees).

chunks.en: "I take upon myself a bull":
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a bull as a burnt offering or peace offering,

chunks.en: he must bring it with its nesachim worth a maneh.
chunks.st: must bring the bull, its accompanying meal offering, and its libations, with the total value of one hundred dinars.

chunks.en: "A calf": he must bring it with its nesachim worth five sela'im.
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a calf, must bring the calf, its accompanying meal offering, and its libations, with the total value of five sela, which equal twenty dinars.

chunks.en: "A ram": he must bring it with its nesachim worth two sela'im.
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a ram, must bring the ram, its accompanying meal offering, and its libations, with the value of two sela, which equal eight dinars.

chunks.en: "A lamb": he must bring it with its nesachim worth one sela.
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a lamb, must bring the lamb, its accompanying meal offering, and its libations, with the value of one sela, which equals four dinars.

words.note: A silver coin worth four dinars.

chunks.en: "A bull worth a maneh":
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a bull with the value of one hundred dinars as a burnt offering or peace offering,

chunks.en: he must bring one worth a maneh, not counting its nesachim.
chunks.st: must bring the bull with the value of one hundred dinars excluding its accompanying meal offering and libations.

chunks.en: "A calf worth five":
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a calf with the value of five sela as a burnt offering or peace offering,

chunks.en: he must bring one worth five, not counting its nesachim.
chunks.st: must bring the calf with the value of five sela excluding its accompanying meal offering and libations.

chunks.en: "A ram worth two":
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a ram with the value of two sela as a burnt offering or peace offering,

chunks.en: he must bring one worth two, not counting its nesachim.
chunks.st: must bring the ram with the value of two sela excluding its accompanying meal offering and libations.

chunks.en: "A lamb worth a sela":
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a lamb with the value of one sela as a burnt offering or peace offering,

chunks.en: he must bring one worth a sela, not counting its nesachim.
chunks.st: must bring the lamb with the value of one sela excluding its accompanying meal offering and libations.

chunks.en: "A bull worth a maneh," and he brought two worth a maneh together,
chunks.st: If one said: It is incumbent upon me to bring a bull with the value of one hundred dinars as a burnt offering or peace offering, and he brought two bulls with a combined value of one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: he has not kept his promise,
chunks.st: he has not fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: even if this one is worth a maneh minus one dinar
chunks.st: And that is the halakha even if this bull has the value of one hundred dinars less one dinar

chunks.en: and that one is worth a maneh minus one dinar.
chunks.st: and that bull has the value of one hundred dinars less one dinar.

chunks.en: "A black one," and he brought a white one,
chunks.st: If one said: It is incumbent upon me to bring a black bull, and he brought a white bull;

chunks.en: "a white one," and he brought a black one,
chunks.st: or said: It is incumbent upon me to bring a white bull, and he brought a black bull;

chunks.en: "a big one," and he brought a small one,
chunks.st: or said: It is incumbent upon me to bring a large bull, and he brought a small bull,

chunks.en: he has not kept his promise.
chunks.st: in all these cases he has not fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: "A small one," and he brought a big one,
chunks.st: But if he said: It is incumbent upon me to bring a small bull, and he brought a large bull,

chunks.en: he has kept it. Rebbi says:
chunks.st: he has fulfilled his obligation, as the value of a small bull is included in the value of a large bull. Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:

chunks.en: He has not kept it.
chunks.st: He has not fulfilled his obligation, as the offering that he brought did not correspond to his vow.

summary: If an animal set aside for an olah got a mum, he may use its redemption money to buy a different number or kind of animal; Rebbi forbids it. If someone said "one of my lambs (or bulls) is hekdesh," the mishnah tells which one becomes holy.

chunks.en: "This bull is an olah,"
chunks.st: With regard to one who said: This bull is hereby a burnt offering, and

chunks.en: and it got a mum: if he wants,
chunks.st: subsequently it became blemished [venista’ev] and was disqualified from sacrifice, he should redeem the bull and with that money purchase another bull as an offering in its stead. If he wishes,

chunks.en: he may bring two with its money.
chunks.st: he may bring two bulls with its redemption money instead of one.

chunks.en: "These two bulls are an olah,"
chunks.st: If one says: These two bulls are hereby a burnt offering, and

chunks.en: and they got a mum: if he wants,
chunks.st: subsequently they became blemished, if he wishes

chunks.en: he may bring one with their money.
chunks.st: he may bring one bull with their redemption money.

chunks.en: Rebbi forbids it.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi deems this prohibited, and holds that he must bring two bulls. In a case where one said:

chunks.en: "This ram is an olah,"
chunks.st: This ram is hereby a burnt offering,

chunks.en: and it got a mum: if he wants,
chunks.st: and it became blemished, if he wishes

chunks.en: he may bring a lamb with its money.
chunks.st: he may bring a lamb with its redemption money. In a case where one said:

chunks.en: "This lamb is an olah," and it got a mum:
chunks.st: This lamb is hereby a burnt offering, and it became blemished,

chunks.en: if he wants,
chunks.st: if he wishes

chunks.en: he may bring a ram with its money.
chunks.st: he may bring a ram with its redemption money.

chunks.en: Rebbi forbids it.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi deems it prohibited for one to bring one type of animal with redemption money from another type of animal.

chunks.en: One who says, "One of my lambs is hekdesh,"
chunks.st: With regard to one who says: One of my lambs is consecrated,

chunks.en: or "One of my bulls is hekdesh":
chunks.st: or: One of my bulls is consecrated,

chunks.en: if he had two,
chunks.st: and he has two lambs or bulls,

chunks.en: the bigger of them is hekdesh.
chunks.st: the larger of them is consecrated.

chunks.en: If three, the middle one of them is hekdesh.
chunks.st: If he has three lambs or bulls, the middle-sized animal among them is consecrated.

chunks.en: "I said which one, but I do not know which I said,"
chunks.st: If one says: I specified the lamb or bull that is to be consecrated but I do not know what animal I specified in my vow,

chunks.en: or he said,
chunks.st: or he says

chunks.he: אָמַר לִי אַבָּא וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מָה,
chunks.en: "My father told me, but I do not know which,"
chunks.st: that: My father said to me before his death that he consecrated one of the lambs or the bulls, but I do not know what animal he consecrated,

chunks.en: the biggest of them is hekdesh.
chunks.st: the largest of them is consecrated.

summary: Korbanos must be brought in the Beis HaMikdash in Yerushalayim, not in the temple of Chonyo in Mitzrayim. Kohanim who served there may not serve in the Beis HaMikdash, but like Kohanim with a mum, they get a share of the korbanos and eat it.

chunks.en: "I take upon myself an olah":
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a burnt offering,

chunks.en: he must bring it in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: must sacrifice it in the Temple in Jerusalem.

chunks.en: And if he brought it in the temple of Chonyo,
chunks.st: And if he sacrificed it in the temple of Onias in Egypt,

words.note: A temple built in Mitzrayim that was not allowed.

chunks.en: he has not kept his promise.
chunks.st: he has not fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: "...that I will bring it in the temple of Chonyo":
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a burnt offering that I will sacrifice in the temple of Onias,

chunks.en: he must bring it in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: must sacrifice it in the Temple in Jerusalem,

chunks.en: But if he brought it in the temple of Chonyo,
chunks.st: but if he sacrificed it in the temple of Onias,

chunks.en: he has kept his promise. Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: he has fulfilled his obligation. Rabbi Shimon says

chunks.en: This is not an olah.
chunks.st: that if one says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a burnt offering that I will sacrifice in the temple of Onias, it is not consecrated as a burnt offering; such a statement does not consecrate the animal at all. If one says:

chunks.en: "I am a nazir":
chunks.st: I am hereby a nazirite,

chunks.en: he must shave in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: then when his term of naziriteship is completed he must shave the hair of his head and bring the requisite offerings in the Temple in Jerusalem;

chunks.en: And if he shaved in the temple of Chonyo,
chunks.st: and if he shaved in the temple of Onias,

chunks.en: he has not kept his promise.
chunks.st: he has not fulfilled his obligation. If one says:

chunks.en: "...that I will shave in the temple of Chonyo":
chunks.st: I am hereby a nazirite provided that I will shave in the temple of Onias,

chunks.en: he must shave in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: he must shave in the Temple in Jerusalem;

chunks.en: But if he shaved in the temple of Chonyo,
chunks.st: but if he shaved in the temple of Onias,

chunks.en: he has kept his promise. Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: he has fulfilled his obligation. Rabbi Shimon says

chunks.en: This person is not a nazir.
chunks.st: that one who says: I am hereby a nazirite provided that I will shave in the temple of Onias, is not a nazirite at all, as his vow does not take effect.

chunks.en: The Kohanim who served in the temple of Chonyo
chunks.st: The priests who served in the temple of Onias

chunks.en: may not serve in the Beis HaMikdash in Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: may not serve in the Temple in Jerusalem;

chunks.en: and of course not if they served something else,
chunks.st: and needless to say, if they served for something else, a euphemism for idolatry, they are disqualified from service in the Temple.

chunks.en: as it says (Melachim II 23):
chunks.st: As it is stated: “

chunks.en: "But the Kohanim of the bamos did not go up
chunks.st: Nevertheless the priests of the private altars did not come up

words.note: Private altars outside the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: to the mizbeach of Hashem in Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem,

chunks.en: only they ate matzos among their brothers."
chunks.st: but they did eat matza among their brethren” (II Kings 23:9).

chunks.en: They are like Kohanim with a mum:
chunks.st: The halakhic status of these priests is like that of blemished priests in that

chunks.en: they get a share and eat,
chunks.st: they receive a share in the distribution of the meat of the offerings and partake of that meat,

chunks.en: but they do not bring korbanos.
chunks.st: but they do not sacrifice offerings or perform any of the sacrificial rites.

summary: The Torah says "a fire offering, a pleasing smell to Hashem" about a big animal olah, a bird, and a small mincha. This teaches that it does not matter whether a person gives a lot or a little, as long as he does it for the sake of Heaven.

chunks.en: It says about the olah of an animal, "a fire offering,
chunks.st: It is stated with regard to an animal burnt offering: “A fire offering,

chunks.en: a pleasing smell" (Vayikra 1),
chunks.st: an aroma pleasing to the Lord” (Leviticus 1:9),

chunks.en: and about the olah of a bird, "a fire offering, a pleasing smell" (there),
chunks.st: and with regard to a bird burnt offering: “A fire offering, an aroma pleasing to the Lord” (Leviticus 1:17),

chunks.en: and about the mincha, "a fire offering, a pleasing smell" (there, 2),
chunks.st: and with regard to a meal offering: “A fire offering, an aroma pleasing to the Lord” (Leviticus 2:2).

chunks.en: to teach that it is the same whether one gives a lot or a little,
chunks.st: The repetitive language employed concerning all of these different offerings is to say to you that one who brings a substantial offering and one who brings a meager offering have equal merit,

words.en: the one who gives a lot
the one who gives a little

chunks.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּכַוֵּן אָדָם אֶת דַּעְתּוֹ לַשָּׁמָיִם:
chunks.en: as long as a person directs his heart to Heaven.
chunks.st: provided that he directs his heart toward Heaven.
